title: Kaden's Story
body:
> ⚡ Know this story cold. On a call you're not just selling a program, you're selling the person behind it. When a prospect hesitates, this story is what closes them. Tell it in your own words, don't recite it.
### Who Is Kaden?
Kaden is the founder of The Grid (MBE Multi Accounting). He runs one of the largest AI-powered multi-account content operations in the space, thousands of accounts posting across platforms, pulling in roughly **100 million views a month** on autopilot, and built it into a business doing around **$100k/month**.
But the reason The Grid exists is what happened before that. Kaden was scaling hard on accounts he didn't control, and one ban wiped out roughly **$70k/month of income overnight**. Everything he'd built lived on a handful of accounts, and when those went down, so did he. He rebuilt from zero, this time with one rule: **never let a single account decide whether you eat.**
He engineered the whole system, the phone builds, the account-creation engine, and the AI distribution layer, so reach is spread across hundreds of accounts instead of concentrated on a few. The Grid is that exact system, installed for agencies and operators who can't afford to get wiped.
### His Philosophy
- **"One account is a single point of failure. Distribution is the only real insurance."** Everyone obsesses over going viral on one account. Kaden's whole thing is the opposite, spread the reach so no single ban touches your income.
- **Bans are not the enemy, dependence is.** Accounts will always go down. The mistake is building where one loss ends you. The Grid makes any single ban a Tuesday, not a disaster.
- **Reach is leverage.** When you can put content everywhere at once on autopilot, you stop renting attention and start owning distribution, the thing every agency and offer actually needs.
- Myths he attacks: "you just need one account to blow up," "getting banned means you did something wrong," "you have to post everything yourself," "this stuff can't be systemized."
### His Results
- **~$100k/month** running the system across a large account network.
- **~100M views/month** on autopilot.
- Rebuilt to that **after** a ban erased ~$70k/month overnight. The comeback is the proof the system works.
- Client and student wins feed the Case Studies page, always match the win to the prospect in front of you.
### Why The Grid Exists
Kaden got burned by the exact problem his clients have: everything riding on accounts they don't control, one ban away from zero. The Grid is what he built so that never happens to him again, and now he installs it for others. Not a course, not tips, the actual system, set up and running, so an agency or operator has reach that survives bans and scales without them touching it.
### Key Talking Points — Use These On Calls
- Founder lost ~$70k/month to a single ban and rebuilt to ~$100k/month by spreading everything across hundreds of accounts. He lived the problem and built the fix.
- ~100M views/month on autopilot, the system runs without him posting.
- The pitch in one line: your reach stops living on one account you could lose tomorrow.
- We install the whole thing, phone builds, account engine, AI distribution. Done-with-you, not a PDF.
### Catchphrases (use his language)
- "One account is a single point of failure."
- "Bans happen. The Grid makes them not matter."
- "Stop renting your reach. Own your distribution."
> 🛡️ COMPLIANCE — NON-NEGOTIABLE: Never say ban-proof, undetectable, or guaranteed. Accounts can and do get banned, that's the honest framing and the whole reason the system exists (resilience, not immunity). Never promise a prospect a view count or a dollar figure. Every proof number is Kaden's or a verified client's. "Results vary." Getting this wrong is a legal liability.
> 🎥 Internal training media (do NOT send to prospects): Kaden telling his story, Kaden on the market and competitors, a client-win walkthrough, and a real sales call. Add the Loom and Drive links here as they're recorded.

title: EODs & Forms SOP
body:
> 📋 Forms are how we see the business. If it isn't logged, it didn't happen. Submit every form the same day, every day you work. No exceptions.
>
> **TIMING STANDARDS:** BOD before your first dial/DM. EODs by 9 PM EST sharp — same day, every day. Set times, set standards.
## 🌅 Sales Rep BOD Form (start of day — EVERYONE)
> ⏰ Fill this out BEFORE your first dial or DM of the day. Takes 60 seconds. The moment you submit is the moment the team knows you're on the clock.
**Form link:** [Sales Rep BOD form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSerd7CiWJycaf5P_eyFjkofqNy_0xBdm4EQzJLM17JvY0CBkg/viewform)
What to report:
- How you're feeling this morning (1–5, be honest — a low score gets you a call from your manager because we actually care, not to punish you)
- Whether you completed your morning routine
- Your ONE non-negotiable for today — specific, and you will be held to it
- The skill you're sharpening today (pull it from what you wrote in yesterday's EOD)
Why this exists: patterns show up in BODs before they show up in your numbers. Three low mornings in a row means something's off, and we'd rather fix it with you on Tuesday than see it in your close rate on Friday.
---
## 📲 Setter EOD Form
Submit at the end of every day you set. This is how we track speed-to-lead and booking rate.
**Form link:** [Setter EOD form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1eVH2l8hdObyVtmgmVCGOFWYrGI7DZhxejVAGKGiwRA4/viewform)

- Total triage calls completed
- Total calls booked today
- Any leads flagged as high priority

- What you're going to do tomorrow to CRUSH (tomorrow's BOD asks you about this)
---

Submit at the end of every single day you work the DMs. This is how we track pitch-to-book rate and show rate on DM-sourced calls.
**Form link:** [DM Setter EOD form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSckZ5cXYqvAvZIxkw0LZBMyaJyipUjcTy6KR1Y6Z3v_vl9Rmg/viewform)

- What you're going to do tomorrow to CRUSH (tomorrow's BOD asks you about this)
---
## 🎯 Closer EOD Form
Submit at the end of every day you take calls.
**Form link:** [Closer EOD form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1-fJjTqBYjdWLfLPEvRLbn2rHEdPv3h1D1vHIr0HosoM/viewform)
What to report:

- Total closes
- Total no-closes (with reasons)

## 📝 Closer Post-Call Notes Form
> ⏱️ Fill this out IMMEDIATELY after every single call, closed or not. Do not wait until end of day. Your notes are the next rep's starting point and the whole team's memory of that lead.

title: Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) Cheatsheet
body:
> 🎯 Who you're actually talking to. Diagnose which one they are in the first few minutes, then mirror their language back to them.
## The core ICP
Operators and agencies who need reach at scale and are one ban away from losing it. They already have something going, an offer, an agency, a content operation, and they've felt the pain of everything riding on accounts they don't control.
## The buyer types
**1. The agency owner scaling content.** Runs client accounts or their own, needs volume and reach, keeps hitting account limits and bans. Pain: growth capped by how many accounts survive. Language: "reach," "scale," "clients," "getting flagged."
**2. The operator who got wiped.** Was making real money, took a ban, lost a chunk of income overnight. Pain: fear it happens again, everything on too few accounts. Language: "banned," "lost it all," "started over." This one closes on Kaden's story, he lived exactly this.
**3. The offer owner who needs distribution.** Has a product/offer but can't get enough eyes on it. Pain: dependent on one platform or one account for all their traffic. Language: "views," "attention," "can't get seen."
## Green flags (book / close them)
- Already running an operation and has resources to invest in an install.
- Has been burned by a ban or is scared of the single-point-of-failure.
- Decisive and can start soon.
## Red flags (disqualify or flag hard)
- No budget and no ability to get one.
- Wants a magic button, "guaranteed" viral, or "guaranteed" no bans, we don't sell that.
- Can't explain what they actually do or why they want this.
- Just curious, no intent.
## The pain that closes them
Every buyer type shares one nightmare: everything they've built lives on accounts they don't control, and one ban ends it. The Grid's whole promise answers that, distribution they own, reach that survives any single ban.
> 🛡️ Mirror their pain, never their fantasy. Never agree that we'll make them "ban-proof" or "guaranteed" anything. Sell resilience and distribution. "Results vary."

title: Objection Handling Cheat Sheet
body:
> 🎯 **The one rule:** an objection is not a no, it's a request for more certainty. You never argue. Your job is to make the yes feel safe. Calm, curious, on their side, the big brother who's already been where they are, not a guru pushing them.
## The Method — run every objection through this
**Listen fully → Acknowledge → Isolate → Reframe → Confirm & close.**
1. **Listen fully.** Let them finish. Silence pulls out the real objection, which usually comes second.
2. **Acknowledge.** "That's fair." "I get it." Never say "but."
3. **Isolate.** *"If that weren't an issue, is this a yes?"* If yes, solve that one thing. If no, dig deeper.
4. **Reframe.** Change how they see it with proof, logic, or a story. Change the frame, don't fight the fact.
5. **Confirm & close.** "Does that make sense?" then move straight to the next step.
> 🧠 **Every objection is 1 of 3 roots, diagnose before answering:** ① "does this work?" (vehicle → mechanism + proof) · ② "will it work for ME?" (self → case study of someone just like them) · ③ "do I trust you?" (burned → track record + honesty + risk reversal).
> 🔥 Run the **Perspective Shift** BEFORE they object (Scripts Hub, Phase 2). Most objections never happen if you did it right.
---
## 🔑 The Grid-specific objections
### "Isn't this against the rules? Won't my accounts just get banned?"
**Root:** ③ trust + risk fear. **Handle it honest.**
"Straight up, anyone who tells you an account can never get banned is lying to you. Bans happen. That's the whole reason this exists. The Grid isn't about pretending you won't get hit, it's about making it not matter. When your reach is spread across hundreds of accounts, one going down is a Tuesday, not a disaster. You stop betting everything on accounts you don't control. That's the entire idea."
> 🚨 NEVER say ban-proof, undetectable, or "you won't get banned." Always resilience + diversification framing. Hard legal line.
### "Can't I just do this myself / learn it for free?"
**Root:** ① value. "You could try. Most people who piece it together burn months and a lot of cash getting phones, software, and accounts to survive at scale, and most quit when the accounts die. You're not paying for information, you're paying for the exact system Kaden runs thousands of accounts on, already working, so you skip the year of trial and error."
### "Will this even work for my niche?"
**Root:** ② fit. "What are you running right now? … The system doesn't care about the niche, it cares about distribution, and distribution works everywhere. We've got operators in spots a lot like yours doing exactly this. Here's someone who started where you are." (Case study LIKE them, not the biggest number.)
### "I don't have time for this"
"That's the whole point. It runs on autopilot, the AI does the distribution. Kaden runs thousands of accounts and doesn't post one himself. The setup is the work, then it runs without you."
---
## 💬 General objections
### "I need to think about it"
Hidden objection. "Totally fair, what specifically do you want to think through? Let's talk it out right now, I'd rather answer it here than have you sit on it alone." Then isolate: "Is it more the money, the timing, or whether this'll actually work for you?"
### "I can't afford it / too expensive"
Re-anchor to the outcome BEFORE any number: "If money wasn't the issue, would this be a yes? … Compared to what? You're one ban from losing what you make right now. This is the thing that means that never wipes you out again, and it scales your reach on top."
> ⚠️ A payment plan may exist, never improvise terms, confirm with Daniel. Never drop price naked.
### "How do I know this isn't a scam / that you're legit?"
"Good, you should ask. Kaden got wiped out, lost $70k a month in a day, and rebuilt to around $100k a month running thousands of accounts, roughly 100M views a month. He lives this. And I'll tell you the same thing we tell everyone: nobody can promise you a result, we show you the system and the receipts, you do the work."
### "I've tried things before and they didn't work"
"Appreciate you being straight. What'd you try, and what was missing? … Most stuff hands you information and leaves you to figure out scale alone, that's where people drown. The system, the phone builds, the account engine, the AI distribution, that's the part we actually run with you."
### "I need to talk to my spouse / partner"
"Totally get it, is it the decision itself or just looping them in? … Want to grab them for 10 minutes right now so I can answer both your questions?" If unavailable, frame the cost of waiting and lock a firm follow-up with both on.
---
> 🔗 This page = what to SAY. How to run the CRM, dials, and no-shows lives in the other Closers SOPs pages.

title: Multi-Accounting Terminology
body:
> 📖 Speak the language. If you sound like you actually understand the operation, prospects trust you. If you fumble the terms, you lose them. Learn these cold.
## Core terms
- **Phone farm** — a rack of physical devices running many accounts at once to post and distribute content at scale.
- **Multi-accounting** — running many accounts in parallel instead of one, so reach and risk are spread out.
- **The network / the grid** — the full set of accounts an operator runs together as one distribution machine.
- **Distribution** — getting the same content out across many accounts and platforms at once. The whole game. Reach you own, not reach you rent.
- **Account warming** — aging and building trust on a new account before pushing volume, so it survives longer.
- **Aged accounts** — older, established accounts that are more resilient and reach further than fresh ones.
- **Ban / wipe** — when a platform takes down an account or many at once. The risk the whole system is built to make survivable.
- **Single point of failure** — when everything rides on one account, so one ban ends you. The exact problem The Grid solves.
- **Autopilot** — the AI distribution layer posting across the network without the operator posting manually.
- **Proxies** — tools that give accounts separate network identities so the farm runs cleanly at scale.
> 🛡️ How to talk about bans: always as resilience, never immunity. "No single ban touches your income," never "you won't get banned" or "ban-proof." That framing is both the honest truth and the compliance line.

title: No-Close Process
body:
> 🔄 A no-close is not a no. It's a not-yet. Most people who don't buy on the call buy later IF you run the follow-up right. The fortune is in the follow-up, and the follow-up starts the second the call ends.
## The second the call ends
1. **Log it in Close immediately** — status to **No-Close / Follow-Up**, not left as "Showed."
2. **Fill Post-Call Notes** while it's fresh: the REAL objection (money / trust / "will it work for me"), where their head's at, and the exact next step + date.
3. **Set the follow-up task** in Close with a due date. If it's not scheduled, it won't happen.
## The follow-up cadence
- **Same day:** a short human text. "Hey [Name], really enjoyed the call. No pressure at all, I just think this actually fixes the thing you're stuck on. What's the one thing still on your mind?" (Re-open, don't chase.)
- **Day 2–3:** send a piece of proof that matches THEIR situation (a case study, a screen recording), not a "you still interested?" text.
- **Day 4–7:** call again. Isolate the real objection and handle it with the Objection Handling Cheat Sheet.
- **Ongoing:** if they go quiet, they drop into the **Kit Follow-Up sequence** which keeps nurturing for weeks. Your job is to keep the human touches going on the warm ones.
> 🧠 Diagnose before you follow up: was it vehicle ("does this work?"), self ("will it work for me?"), or trust ("do I believe you?")? Your follow-up should attack the ACTUAL root, not just "circle back." (See Objection Handling Cheat Sheet.)
> 🛡️ Never invent urgency or fake a "price goes up tonight" to force a no-close. And never promise a result or that they won't get banned to save a deal. We close on truth or we don't close.

title: Setter Playbook & Triage Script
body:
> ⚡ **Speed-to-lead is the whole job. 5 minutes from application, every time.** A lead that applies and hears nothing for an hour is a dead lead. Double-dial, then text. Your note quality IS the closer's performance, write it like the closer is reading your mind.
## Your role
Applications come in through the funnel ([mbemultiaccounting.com/apply](http://mbemultiaccounting.com/apply) → iClosed). You call fast, qualify, and get them booked and SHOWN onto the closer's calendar. You are the first human they talk to. Calm, sharp, on their side.
## 🔁 The daily rhythm
1. Work the Close smart view "New – needs first call" top to bottom.
2. New application → call within **5 minutes**. No answer → call again (double-dial). Still no answer → text using the speed-to-lead template, then log and set a follow-up.
3. Every touch gets logged in Close. Every booked call gets full notes.
4. End of day → submit the **Setter EOD form**.
## 🎯 The triage call — 7 steps
> 🗣️ Spoken, not read. Contractions, short lines, [Name], real pauses. You're a person who's curious about their situation, not a robot reading a form.
**1. Greeting** — "Hey [Name], it's [You] with The Grid, you just put in an application, that's why I'm calling. Caught you at an ok time?"
**2. Frame** — "Cool, so this'll be quick. I just wanna understand what you've got going on and see if this is even a fit, and if it is I'll get you locked in with [Closer] who'll walk you through the whole system. Sound good?"
**3. Qualify** — "So what are you running right now? … How are you getting reach today, one account, a few? … You ever been banned or watched an account just die on you?" (Listen for the real pain: got wiped, everything on one account, can't scale.)
**4. Financial qualify** — done with buckets, never a price. "This is an install-the-whole-system thing, people usually come in ready to invest in the setup to get it running. When you're serious about a project like this, are you in a spot to put real resources behind it, or would that be a stretch right now?" (Gauge, don't quote. Closer owns price.)
**5. Redirect** — if they push for price/details: "Totally get it, that's exactly what [Closer] walks you through on the call, they'll map it to your exact situation. My job's just to make sure it's a fit and get you in front of them."
**6. Rapport** — one genuine human beat. React to something they said. Make them feel understood, not processed.
**7. Book** — "Alright, you're a fit. I'm putting you in with [Closer] for [day/time], that work? … You'll get a text and email confirmation. Do me a favor and actually show up on time, [Closer] blocks this time just for you. Anything comes up, hit me and we'll move it."
> 🚫 Never quote a price. Never promise a result or that they won't get banned. Never say ban-proof / guaranteed. You qualify and book, the closer sells.
## 📝 Note quality standard (non-negotiable)
After every triage call, the closer should be able to read your notes and know exactly who's walking in. Log:
- What they run now + how they get reach today
- Their real pain (the thing that actually stings, in their words)
- Financial read (bucket, not a number) + urgency
- Any objection or hesitation you already heard
- One personal detail for rapport
> 🔗 Weak notes = the closer walks in blind = the deal dies. This is the single highest-leverage thing you do. Speed-to-lead templates + no-show follow-up cadence live in the Closers SOPs → No-Show Process page.

title: Sales Calls Recordings
body:
> 🎟️ Record every call. It's how you get better, how we coach you, and how we build the objection library. No recording = no review = no improvement.
## The rule
- **Every** call gets recorded, closes and no-closes both. The no-closes teach us the most.
- Recordings live in the Master Drive, in the sales-call-recordings folder.
- Name each file: Date – Prospect Name – Outcome (e.g. 2026-07-26 – John D – No-Close).
## What we do with them
- **Call Review** (see the team meeting schedule): we pull real calls and break down what worked and what didn't.
- Your best closes become training for new reps. Your toughest objections feed the Objection Handling Cheat Sheet.
- Before a call review, flag the one call you most want eyes on.
> 🛡️ Recordings are internal training only. Never send a raw sales call to a prospect. Client-facing proof (wins, screenshots) is a separate, approved set.

title: Close CRM SOP
body:
> 🗄️ Close is the source of truth. If it's not in Close, it didn't happen. Update the lead the moment anything changes, not at end of day.
## Your smart views (org-shared, already built)
Work them top to bottom, every day:
- **New – needs first call** — fresh applications. Speed-to-lead 5 min.
- **Booked – upcoming calls** — your calendar. Prep each (see Pre-Call Process).
- **No-show – follow up** — run the no-show cadence.
- **Follow-up – pending** — warm no-closes with a next step + date.
## 🔄 Every call → update the lead
1. Set the **status** to where they actually are (New → Contacted → Call Booked → Showed → Won / Lost / No-Show, etc.).
2. Fill the **qualifier fields** from the iClosed booking (Business Type, Reach, Goal, Biggest Blocker, Budget, Timeline) if the sync didn't already.
3. Log the **call outcome** in the activity + your notes.
4. Closed? → status Won + submit the **New Deal Log**. Lost? → status Lost with the reason.
> 🔔 Booked calls, closes, and payments auto-post to the matching Slack channel (3-calls-booked, 5-payment-success). Don't double-post by hand, just keep Close accurate and the automations fire.
> 🛡️ Clean data is compliance too. Log what was actually said and promised, nothing inflated. Never record a guarantee you didn't make, because we don't make them.

title: Close CRM SOPs (Setters)
body:
> 🗄️ Close is your command center. Work it top to bottom every day. If a touch isn't logged, it didn't happen, and you won't get commission credit for it.
## Your daily view
- Work the **"New – needs first call"** smart view to zero, every day. Newest applications first, speed-to-lead under 5 min.
- Then work follow-ups and any callbacks you scheduled.
## Every touch → log it
1. Update the lead **status** as it moves (New → Contacted → Call Booked → No-Show / Follow-Up).
2. Log the call/text as an activity, every attempt, every time.
3. On a booked call, write the **full notes** (business, real pain, financial read, hesitations, one rapport detail).
4. Booked a call? Status = **Call Booked** and confirm it's on the right closer's calendar.
> 🔔 Booked calls auto-post to the 3-calls-booked Slack channel off your Close update. Keep Close clean and the automations fire, don't double-post by hand.
> 📝 Your note quality is the closer's performance. Weak notes = the closer walks in blind = the deal dies. This is the highest-leverage thing you do.

title: No-Show Process
body:
> ⚡ A no-show is not a lost lead, it's a lead you haven't reached yet. Most no-shows rebook if you move fast and stay human. Work the "No-show – follow up" smart view every day.
## The cadence (run it fast)
**T + 2 min (missed the call):** call them. "Hey [Name], it's [You] with The Grid, we were set for right now, everything ok? I've got you, let's just find another time."
**T + 5 min:** no answer → text. "Hey [Name], [You] from The Grid, we had our call booked for [time], I know things come up. Want me to grab you the next open slot today? Here's the link: [mbemultiaccounting.com/apply](http://mbemultiaccounting.com/apply)"
**Same day, +3–4 hrs:** second call + text if still nothing.
**Day 2:** one more call + a value/proof text (send a case study, not pressure).
**Day 3–4:** final text, then drop to the long-term follow-up / Kit nurture.
> 🗣️ Tone: never guilt-trip. "I know things come up" beats "you missed our call." You're the person making it easy for them to show up, not scolding them.
> 🔁 Every attempt gets logged in Close. Rebook → status back to Call Booked. Gone cold after the full cadence → mark it and let the Kit No-Show sequence carry them.

title: Dialer & Call Cadence
body:
> ⚡ Speed is the whole job. A lead is hottest the minute they apply and cools fast. 5 minutes, not 50.
## The cadence on a new application
1. **Call within 5 minutes.** No answer →
2. **Double-dial** (call right back, back-to-back often gets picked up). No answer →
3. **Text** the speed-to-lead template (see SMS Templates), then log + set a callback task.
4. **Same day:** 1–2 more attempts spaced out. Mix call + text.
5. **Days 2–4:** keep attempting with a value angle, then let the Kit nurture carry the cold ones.
## Reps
- Watch the time zone before you dial, don't call at 6am their time.
- Leave a short, warm voicemail on the first miss: who you are, why, and that you'll text.
- Log **every** attempt in Close. Attempts you don't log don't count.
> 🔗 Full no-show follow-up cadence lives in Closers SOPs → No-Show Process. Text templates live in SMS Templates.

title: Performance Standards
body:
> 📊 The standard is the standard. These aren't stretch goals, they're the baseline to keep your seat. We coach hard and we hold the line.
## Setters
- **Speed-to-lead: under 5 minutes**, every application. The single biggest lever, non-negotiable.
- Double-dial every new lead, then text. Work the "needs first call" view to zero daily.
- Full, high-quality notes on every booked call (setter notes = closer performance).
- Submit the Setter EOD every day you work.
- Hit your daily dial and booked-call targets set with your manager.
## Closers
- Be early and set up (camera on, quiet room, links ready) for every call.
- Post-Call Notes filled immediately after every call, closed or not.
- Run the No-Show and No-Close cadences, no lead left cold.
- Submit the Closer EOD every day you take calls.
- Hold your show-rate and close-rate targets set with your manager.
## Everyone
- Show up to the AM huddle, call reviews, and weekly review (see schedule).
- Keep Close accurate in real time. If it's not in Close, it didn't happen.
- Know The Offer, Kaden's Story, and the numbers cold.
> 🛡️ One standard we never bend: compliance. Never say ban-proof / undetectable / guaranteed, never promise a result. Breaking a compliance rule is the fastest way off the team, it's a legal liability for the client.

title: SMS Templates
body:

## Speed-to-lead (no answer on first call)

title: Fundamental Checklist / Qualifications
body:
> ✅ Your job is to book FITS, not bodies. A qualified call the closer can actually win beats five tire-kickers. Run every lead against this before you book.
## Who's a fit (book them)
- Runs an agency, offer, or content operation that needs reach at scale (or is scaling paid/organic and keeps hitting account limits/bans).
- Has been burned by a ban or is scared of everything sitting on one account.
- Has real resources to invest in an install (gauge with buckets, never a number).
- Serious, decisive, can start soon.
## Red flags (don't book, or flag hard in notes)
- No budget and no ability to get one, wants it for free.
- Wants a magic button / "guaranteed" viral / "guaranteed" no bans. (We don't sell that.)
- Can't articulate what they actually do or why they want this.
- Tire-kicker just "curious."
## Must-have before you book
- Confirmed name, phone, email, time zone.
- The real pain in their words.
- A financial read (bucket, not a price).
- Full notes in Close so the closer walks in knowing them.
> 🧠 Financial qualify with buckets and framing, never a price. The closer owns the number. (See the Setter Playbook & Triage Script.)

title: Client Onboarding Process
body:
> 🎉 You closed. Now make the handoff clean, the first 10 minutes after "yes" set the tone for the whole relationship. Do these steps in order, on the call if you can.
## The moment they say yes
1. **Collect payment** — send the Fanbasis payment link and get it done on the call. Don't hang up on "I'll pay later."
2. **Send the agreement** — generate The Grid Program Agreement in PandaDoc and get it signed.
3. **Log the New Deal** — submit the [New Deal Log](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1SnSkeMjO_0Oh7VddJDjrXxYki9LBhC3-MWGIHOymZn0/viewform). This fires the payment-success flow and drops the win in Slack. Credit the setter.
4. **Set status to Won** in Close.
5. **Get them into Discord** — send [discord.gg/mbe](https://discord.gg/mbe) and make sure they join before you end the call.

## The handoff to fulfillment
> 🔧 The Grid is a done-with-you install, the fulfillment side builds out their phones, accounts, and distribution. Your job is a clean handoff so the build starts fast.
- Confirm their contact and best communication channel and note it in Close.
- Kit's Client Onboarding sequence auto-runs and walks them through first steps.
- Flag the new client in the payments/onboarding Slack channel so fulfillment picks them up.
> 💡 First win = best proof. The moment this client hits an early result, capture it (screenshot + one line) and drop it in Slack so it feeds Case Studies.

title: Scripts Hub
body:
> 📝 The exact scripts your setters and closers run on every call. The structure never changes, the words are yours. Don't recite, execute.
---
## 📞 Setter Script — The Grid
> 🎯 Objective: triage the lead, qualify intent + finances, build curiosity, and book the call. You're not the closer, your job is to qualify and get them on the calendar with great notes.
**1. Greeting + curiosity** — "Hey [Name], it's [You] with The Grid, you just put in an application, that's why I'm calling. Caught you at an ok time?"
**2. Frame the call** — "This'll be quick. I just wanna understand what you've got going on and see if it's even a fit, and if it is I'll get you locked in with [Closer] who walks you through the whole system. Sound good?"
**3. Qualify** — "What are you running right now? … How are you getting reach today, one account, a few? … You ever been banned or watched an account just die on you?" (Listen for the real pain: got wiped, everything on one account, can't scale.)
**4. Financial qualify (buckets, never a price)** — "This is an install-the-whole-system thing, people come in ready to invest in the setup to get it running. When you're serious about a project like this, are you in a spot to put real resources behind it, or would that be a stretch right now?"
**5. Redirect** — if they push for price/details: "That's exactly what [Closer] walks you through, they map it to your exact situation. My job's just to make sure it's a fit and get you in front of them."
**6. Rapport** — one genuine human beat. React to something they said.
**7. Book** — "Alright, you're a fit. I'm putting you with [Closer] for [day/time], that work? You'll get a text + email confirmation. Show up on time, they block that slot just for you."
> 📝 Log full notes in Close immediately after the call. Setter note quality = closer performance. Never quote a price, never promise a result or that they won't get banned.
---
## 🎯 Closer Script — The Grid
> 🚨 Phase 2 (Perspective Shift) is the single most important step. Do it BEFORE you pitch. Skip it and the close dies.
### Phase 1 — Rapport (5–10 min)
- "Tell me about what you're running right now, what does your operation actually look like?"
- "How's your reach been, you ever been banned or watched an account just die on you?"
- "What made you book this call specifically?"
Get them talking. Listen for the real pain (got wiped, everything on one account, scared it happens again), not the surface answer.
### Phase 2 — Perspective Shift (2–3 min) · the most critical step
"[Name], honest question. You've been thinking about not being one ban away from zero for a while now. What do you think has actually stopped you from fixing it? … And if you keep running everything through accounts you don't control, where are you when the next ban hits, same spot, starting over? … So the real question isn't whether you want this, you clearly do. It's whether you fix it now or wait until you get wiped again. I'm not judging, I just want to know who I'm talking to."
### Phase 3 — Pitch Transition (1–2 min)
"I appreciate you being real with me. Let me show you exactly what Kaden built and why it fixes the thing you've been stuck on."
### Phase 4 — The Pitch
- **What it is:** The Grid installs the whole system, the phone builds, the account-creation engine, and the AI distribution layer, so hundreds of accounts run on autopilot and your reach lives everywhere instead of on one account you could lose tomorrow.
- **The proof (show it):** thousands of accounts posting daily, ~100M views/month on this exact system. Kaden rebuilt to ~$100k/month after a ban wiped ~$70k/month overnight.
- **Tie it to them:** connect ONE proof point to their exact situation from discovery.
- **The offer:** present the tier that fits their operation (see The Offer). Present the price confidently. Don't apologize for it.
### Phase 5 — Close + Objections
- "Based on everything we talked about, does this make sense for where you're at?"
- "What's the one thing you'd need answered before you get started?"
- Handle objections with the **Objection Handling Cheat Sheet** (Closers SOPs).
- Final ask: "Alright [Name], let's get you set up, I'll send you the link right now."
> 🛡️ Compliance: never say ban-proof, undetectable, or guaranteed. Never promise a prospect a dollar or that they won't get banned. Frame everything as resilience and distribution, no single ban touches your income. Every proof number is Kaden's or a verified client's. "Results vary."

title: Pre-Call Process
body:
> 🎯 You win the call before it starts. Never walk in cold. 5 minutes of prep changes the whole conversation.
## Before every call
1. **Read the setter's notes + iClosed answers.** Know their business, their reach, their real pain, their budget read, and any hesitation before you say hello.
2. **Pick your proof.** Choose the ONE case study / proof point that looks most like THEM (see Case Studies). Have it ready to show.
3. **Pre-load the Perspective Shift.** Based on their notes, know the gap you're going to make them admit (Scripts Hub, Phase 2).
4. **Anticipate the objection.** From the notes, you usually already know if it'll be money, trust, or "will it work for me" — have that response loaded (Objection Cheat Sheet).
5. **Be early + set up.** Camera on, quiet room, link + payment link ready so a yes closes on the spot, no fumbling.
> 🔗 Then run the 5-phase script (Scripts Hub). Prep tees up the Perspective Shift, the script does the rest.

title: Compensation & Pay Structure
body:
> 💰 Straight and transparent. You're a 1099 contractor. You get paid on results, cash that's actually collected. The better you perform, the more you make. No caps.
## The splits
- **Setters: 5%** of collected revenue on deals you booked that close.
- **Closers: 10%** of collected revenue on deals you close.
- Paid on **cash collected**, not contracted. On a payment plan, you're paid as the client actually pays.
## How it's tracked
- Every close is logged in the **New Deal Log** with the setter credited, that's how commission is attributed. Log it right or you don't get credited.
- Payments run through Fanbasis, and the tracking sheet auto-calculates the 5% / 10% commission on collected cash.
- Commissions pay out on the team's regular payout schedule.
- Attribution disputes: raise it in Slack the same day, we settle it off the New Deal Log and Close records.
> 🔗 Your comp is a direct function of the standards on the Performance Standards page. Hit the activity, hit the pay.
